userStories.title: SQLite with verified WAL and FTS5, Alembic baseline and health routes
userStories.description: Add persistence: a synchronous SQLAlchemy 2.1 engine (ADR 0009) for the single SQLite writer (ADR 0004) in the data volume, WAL and FTS5 verified at startup, an Alembic baseline migration, and `GET /health/live` and `GET /health/ready` of docs/api.md. Fill the backend part of `test integration`.
acceptanceCriteria: At startup the backend verifies WAL mode and FTS5 and refuses to become ready otherwise; an integration test in the real backend image proves both.
`alembic upgrade head` creates the baseline on an empty database, and a migration test checks it.
`GET /health/live` answers 200, and `GET /health/ready` reports database, migrations and FTS5, with the control API reported separately.
`scripts\lyrveil.cmd test integration` runs the backend integration tests in the test stage.
userStories.notes:
Added the SQLite persistence layer, the Alembic baseline, the health routes and the backend `test integration` level. `test integration` passed (20 tests), `test unit tests/unit` passed (39), and `test lint` passed after fixes. I did not run the Pester tests, including the one I added, and I did not start the runtime image. The new unit and integration tests run in the test stage; that stage shares the runtime's base image, but I never compared the two SQLite builds directly.

- **Engine:** `persistence/database.py` builds a synchronous SQLAlchemy 2.1 engine that applies the five documented pragmas on every connection. It uses manual transactions, so a `WRITE` option gives `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`.
- **Startup check:** `verify_capabilities` reads back the journal mode SQLite reports and creates a temporary `fts5` table. It raises `DatabaseCapabilityError` (`DB_CAPABILITY_MISSING`) when either is missing.
- **Startup behaviour:** `main()` runs that check and then migrates. If the check fails, or the file cannot be opened or migrated, it logs the reason and returns 69 without starting the server.
- **Migrations:** `persistence/migrations.py`, `alembic.ini` and `migrations/` with baseline `0001`, which creates `application_settings` only. `alembic -x database=<path> upgrade head` works from the command line, and `upgrade_to_head` does the same in code.
- **Health routes:**
  - `GET /api/v1/health/live` answers 200.
  - `GET /api/v1/health/ready` checks the database and WAL, the migrations and FTS5 on every request. It answers 200 or 503, and reports the control API separately in `control_api.reachable`, which never changes the status.
  - The control API is probed with `GET /v1/health` at `lyrveil-orchestrator:8100`.
- **Dependencies and image:** `uv.lock` regenerated in a container with SQLAlchemy 2.1.6 and Alembic 1.20.1; no existing pin changed. The test and runtime stages now copy `alembic.ini` and `migrations/`.
- **Test runner:** `test integration` builds the test stage and runs `pytest tests/integration` without network. I added a Pester case for the integration level in a fixture with no Python component.
- **Tests:** 20 integration tests and 8 unit tests.
- **Docs:** `backend.md`, `testing.md`, `api.md`, `data-model.md`, `docs/README.md`, the roadmap evidence list, `CHANGELOG.md` and a new verification file. The roadmap checkbox is left for the orchestrator.

userStories.notes: ContainerGate (orchestrator/src/lyrveil_orchestrator/container_gate.py) is the only user of the Docker socket. userStories.title: GPU monitor, preflight and the control API with its token
userStories.description: Implement `gpu_monitor.py` (`GPUResourceMonitor` over NVML with nvidia-ml-py behind the `GpuProbe` port), `preflight.py` (the orchestrator's rows of the preflight table in docs/operations.md, runnable as `python -m lyrveil_orchestrator.preflight`), and `api.py`, the control API of docs/api.md that requires `Authorization: Bearer <LYRVEIL_CONTROL_TOKEN>` on every route except `/v1/health`.
acceptanceCriteria: T-ORC-10 passes: a missing or wrong token gets 401 on every route except `/v1/health`, and tokens are compared in constant time.

userStories.notes: Delivered P01.4c in the orchestrator. `gpu_monitor.py` defines the `GpuProbe` port, `NvmlProbe` (makes only the documented NVML calls on device 0, rounds to MiB, raises `GpuProbeError` for any NVML failure including a missing library, and retries init on the next read) and `GPUResourceMonitor`. `preflight.py` judges the four orchestrator rows at the thresholds in docs/operations.md: CUDA at least 13.0, total VRAM pass from 11000 MiB, warning from 10000, failure below that; free VRAM pass from 9000 MiB, otherwise a warning, with a waiting note below 6000 and never a failure. When NVML fails, all four rows fail. It runs as `python -m lyrveil_orchestrator.preflight [--json]` and exits 0 with only warnings, 1 when a row fails. `api.py` has `create_app(control_token, monitor)`, which refuses a token that is not 64 hex characters. Middleware runs before routing and requires a Bearer token on every path except `GET /v1/health`, compared with `hmac.compare_digest`. Any failure gets the same 401 problem response with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`. `GET /v1/preflight` returns the report. OpenAPI and docs pages are off. Added FastAPI 0.162.0 and nvidia-ml-py 13.615.71, held Pydantic at 2.14.2 with `constraint-dependencies`, and regenerated uv.lock through the Dockerfile lockfile stage. Created orchestrator/tests/integration, which `test integration` picks up on its own. userStories.notes:
I created `frontend/`: a standalone Angular 22.2.4 app (CLI and build 22.2.5, TypeScript 6.0.3) with zoneless change detection set explicitly. Its route table covers the 13 documented screens. `/` and unknown paths go to `/chats`. Each screen loads lazily as a placeholder that shows its title and says it is not available yet.

The design tokens are in `src/styles/tokens.scss`, and the reset, typography and global stylesheets build on them. All three font families are bundled locally from the `@fontsource` packages at 5.3.0.

The text catalog is `src/i18n/it.json`, imported directly into the code so it works offline. The `Translator` service derives the key types from the catalog, so a wrong key fails the build. userStories.description: Implement the local-only checks of docs/security.md and ADR 0017: the backend refuses a Host or Origin that is not the local app, on REST and on the WebSocket handshake, and the backend and `nginx.conf` set the documented security headers on every response. If no WebSocket route exists yet, add the realtime endpoint of docs/api.md with its handshake only; P02.5c adds the events.

userStories.notes:
The backend now refuses requests that don't come from the local app. A request whose Host is not localhost or 127.0.0.1 on LYRVEIL_HTTP_PORT gets 403 FORBIDDEN_ORIGIN as application/problem+json. So does a write (any method other than GET or HEAD) or a /ws handshake that carries a foreign Origin. This works on REST and on the WebSocket handshake; the refusal body and the log never repeat the refused value. Both the backend and nginx.conf send the six documented security headers on every answer, errors included, and nginx removes the backend's copies so each header arrives only once. An unexpected exception now gives a generic 500 INTERNAL that carries the same headers. /ws now accepts the handshake and sends the `connected` frame with a per-process boot_id; events are left for P02.5c.

The allowed lists come from two new properties on Settings, both derived from LYRVEIL_HTTP_PORT: allowed_hosts and allowed_origins. With port 80 the names without a port are also allowed. The backend also accepts Host 127.0.0.1:8000, because the Compose health check connects that way. compose.test.yaml now gives the backend LYRVEIL_HTTP_PORT equal to the test port.

userStories.title: Orchestrator loads and stops the text runtime, with leases
userStories.description: Implement the text-mode part of `lifecycle.py` and `supervisor.py`: start `lyrveil-llm` through `ContainerGate`, wait for readiness, stop it and verify release, and the leases of docs/gpu-orchestration.md (Leases and the global lock). The 18-step image flow is P06.1.
acceptanceCriteria: T-ORC-03 passes: one lease at a time, mode match, expiry and heartbeat.
With `fake_docker` and `fake_nvml`, the orchestrator starts the text runtime from the default mode `llm`, reports `LLM_READY`, and stops it on `POST /v1/drain`, along the state machine table.
The backend's `OrchestratorClient` acquires, renews and releases a lease and handles a refused or expired one.
userStories.notes:
The orchestrator can now start and stop the text runtime and hand out leases. The backend has a client that uses those leases. Lint passes and the new unit tests pass. The new integration test that covers the second acceptance criterion has not run yet.

What was built:
- **`supervisor.py`** (`ProcessSupervisor`): refuses to start a runtime while the other one runs (exclusivity rule 3). It starts `lyrveil-llm` through `ContainerGate` and polls Docker health until `healthy`, failing with `LLM_LOAD_FAILED`, or `RUNTIME_CONFIG_INVALID` when the runtime exits with status 78. On stop it uses the 20 s grace period, then checks `State.Running`, the exit code and `top`. It then samples NVML every 500 ms until three samples lie within 64 MiB, for at most 60 s. The VRAM growth at load and the drop at release are measured; they are recorded but never fail a check.
- **`lifecycle.py`** (`ModelLifecycleManager`): owns the state, the desired mode (default `llm`), the single lease, drain/resume, recover, the event buffer of 5000 and a reduced recovery. It applies one `state_machine.py` transition per step. Lease rules: one at a time (`LEASE_HELD`), mode match with no pending mode change or drain (`NOT_READY`), 30 s ttl renewed by heartbeat, and expiry moves to `RECOVERING` with `LEASE_LOST`. A release with `oom` or `runtime_error` goes to `RECOVERING`. A runtime that loses health ends the lease. A failed load is retried after 5 s and 20 s, and the third failure ends in `ERROR`.
- **`api.py`**: now serves every control route: state with long poll, desired-mode, leases (acquire, heartbeat, release), recover, drain, resume and events. The app's lifespan runs the manager loop. The signature is now `create_app(token, monitor, lifecycle)`, so the existing T-ORC-10 test was updated; its 404 check now targets an unknown path.
- **Backend `OrchestratorClient`** (`lyrveil/orchestration/client.py`): uses only the standard library and ignores proxy settings. `acquire_lease` raises `LeaseRefusedError` with `NOT_READY` or `LEASE_HELD`. `renew_lease` raises `LeaseLostError` on 410. `release_lease` returns False on 410. Anything else raises `OrchestratorUnavailableError`.

- `test lint`: passed for backend, orchestrator, frontend and docs.
- `test unit -k "test_leases or test_supervisor or test_orchestrator_client or test_socket_confinement"`: orchestrator 46 passed, including 11 T-ORC-03 tests and 10 supervisor tests; backend 10 passed.

**Not checked:**
- The `integration` level cannot be filtered, so `tests/integration/test_text_lifecycle.py` (start from mode `llm` → `LLM_READY` → lease → `POST /v1/drain` → `IDLE`) and the updated `test_control_api.py` have not run.

userStories.notes:
I added `PromptFormatter` for `gemma4`, `mistral_v3_tekken` and `chatml` in `backend/src/lyrveil/prompts/formatter.py`, following docs/prompting.md (Prompt format) and ADRs 0025 and 0031.

What it does:
- `formatter_for(family)` returns the formatter for a catalog template.
- `chat(parts, current_message)` lays out a reply prompt: the stable text, the history as plain turns, then the last user turn. That turn holds the frame of the dynamic context and the current message.
- `proactive(parts, instruction)` uses the same layout, but the frame ends with the instruction and has no `[Messaggio di …]` line.
- `structured(system, user)` gives one system text and one user turn, with no frame.
- `stop_sequences(user_display_name)` returns each family's stop list.
- `chat` and `proactive` return `FormattedPrompt(text, prefix)`. `prefix` is the part of `text` before the last user turn: the stable text plus history for `gemma4` and `chatml`, only the history for `mistral_v3_tekken`.
- `neutralize_frame_markers` turns the `[` into `(` on any line starting with `[Contesto per` or `[Messaggio di` (any case, optional leading spaces, also after a lone `\r`). It is applied to every text the formatter receives, so only the formatter itself writes real markers. No family writes BOS.

Tests: `backend/tests/unit/test_prompt_formatter.py` holds 24 cases for T-MOD-02 and T-MOD-05. The golden strings are written from the formats in docs/prompting.md, because sessions have no access to the official templates; T-GPU-03 will confirm them. The tests check:
- the golden strings for chat and structured prompts;
- the stop sequences;
- that no family writes BOS;
- that two consecutive replies share the prefix byte for byte, and old turns carry no frame;
- that markers are neutralized in the summary, user and character turns, memories, the current message and the proactive instruction;
- the proactive layout, empty blocks being dropped, and that neutralizing twice changes nothing.

The final format fix only moved line breaks and came after that test run. I did not run the integration, e2e or Docker levels, or anything against a real model.

Choices the docs did not fix, recorded in docs/backend.md: an empty block 4, 5 or 9 is left out of the frame, and trailing line breaks of a block are dropped. Each history turn is written under its own role, so two character turns in a row produce two `{reply}</s>` pieces in `mistral_v3_tekken`, an order its GGUF template would refuse.

Finding, outside this task: nothing removes control tokens such as `<|turn>`, `[INST]` or `<|im_start|>` that a user types into a message. KoboldCpp reads control tokens written in the prompt as real tokens, so this is a possible prompt injection that no document covers yet.

userStories.title: Durable job queue with retries
userStories.description: Implement `jobs/` as in ADR 0010 and docs/backend.md (Job handlers, Retry policy): jobs stored in SQLite in the same transaction as the change that creates them, priorities, retries with backoff, and recovery after a restart. The scheduling policy across modes is completed in P06.3.
acceptanceCriteria: A job is committed with the change that creates it and survives a restart; interrupted running jobs recover as documented.
Retries follow the documented backoff and maximum, and end in a failed state with its reason.
A job not eligible in the current mode waits instead of running.
userStories.notes:
The durable job queue from ADR 0010 is in place. Revision 0002 creates `generation_jobs` with CHECK lists, json_valid checks, a partial unique index on idempotency_key and the selection index. The `jobs/` package has four modules:
- `policy.py` holds the kinds, priorities, classes, attempts, backoffs and the stage-to-mode mapping.
- `queue.py` holds `JobQueue`. It works on a connection the caller owns and never commits, so a job is committed or rolled back with the change that creates it.
- `handlers.py` defines the handler contract: `JobDone`, `NextStage`, `JobFailedError` and `JobPreemptedError`.
- `scheduler.py` holds `JobScheduler`. It runs one job at a time and only when its stage needs `none` or the mode the GPU is in. A refused or unanswered lease leaves the job queued. It renews the lease every 10 s; a lost lease cancels the handler and retries with LEASE_LOST. Each failure code maps to a lease release outcome (oom, runtime_error or ok).

Retries use the kind's backoff and maximum, then end `failed` with error_code and error_detail. `main()` now requeues interrupted `running` jobs at startup (step 5). The interrupted run counts as an attempt, and a job on its last attempt fails with JOB_INTERRUPTED. `domain/identifiers.py` adds UUIDv7 ids and UTC timestamp text with milliseconds.

Checks I observed:
- `scripts/lyrveil.cmd test lint` passed, after fixing ruff findings and line breaks.
- `test unit tests/unit/test_job_policy.py`: 5 passed.
- `test unit` on tests/integration/test_job_queue.py, test_migrations.py and test_health_and_startup.py: 31 passed. The integration level takes no file arguments, so I ran these files through the unit level's pytest.

userStories.description: Implement messages as in docs/data-model.md and docs/api.md (Messages): send with an idempotency key, committed before its reply job exists, edit, delete, regeneration into variants with alternatives, and history paging.

I did not run the full unit, integration, e2e or docker levels.

**What it does**
- **Send** saves the user message and a queued reply placeholder in one transaction, then queues the `chat_reply` job in a second one. A full queue therefore can't lose the user's text. Retrying with the same `client_message_id` returns the first result, and queues the job if the first attempt died before queuing it.
- **Regenerate** works only on the last visible message, and only when a character wrote it. It adds an active `generated` variant and queues `chat_regenerate`. The old variants stay and can be switched back to with activate.
- **Edit** adds an `edited` variant, and editing to the same text changes nothing. **Delete** is a soft delete.
- **History** returns pages of the newest messages below `before_seq`, oldest first inside each page. Queued, failed and interrupted replies are included with their status.

**Choices I made without a spec**
- Send and regenerate in an archived conversation answer 409.
- The `image` intent answers 409 until P05.
- If the queue is full, the new reply or variant is marked failed and the call answers 409. A retry with the same `client_message_id` queues it again.

Assisted creation now works end to end. `POST /characters/drafts` checks the description (not blank, at most 2000 characters) and queues a `character_draft` job. A completed job's result is `{card, proposed_fields, character_id, attempts}` and no character is written. A new `GET /jobs/{id}` returns a job's state and result but never its payload. In the Creator, a **Bozza assistita** panel queues a draft, polls that route every second showing the queue position, and fills the form without making it the saved state. A note lists the proposed fields by label. Only **Salva personaggio** goes on to save through the normal routes. A failed draft shows the server's reason.

userStories.notes: Implemented the memory extraction pipeline of docs/memory-engine.md and docs/prompting.md. MemoryExtractionService (services/memory_extraction.py) is the memory_extraction handler, registered in the lifespan. The ExtractionResult schema (domain/memory_extraction.py) drives both the GBNF grammar and the validation. The prompt follows extraction.v1 (prompts/extraction.py) with one worked example, at temperature 0.3 and max_length 1200. Windows and triggers are in memory/window.py: up to 12 readable messages after last_extracted_seq, stopping before a pending reply, with 2 earlier messages as context and a window hash over message id, active variant id and content hash. A job is triggered after each stored reply, in its own transaction, when 10 messages are unprocessed (8 to 12 allowed), or 2 when a user message matches prompts/it/significant_patterns.txt. Only one extraction job runs per chat at a time. Idempotency: a run row is written running before generation. A completed window is never generated again; the cursor moves past it. A failed or interrupted run is restarted with attempt + 1. The commit transaction reads the window again and marks the run superseded if it changed; otherwise it writes the memories, sources (message, active variant, content hash), memory_fts rows, episodes with sources, links and episode_fts rows, the completed run with raw_output, and the cursor, then checks the trigger for what is left. Invalid output, refused twice, records the run failed with the refused text and raises a retryable STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_INVALID, so the job retries after 1 and 5 minutes; nothing else changes. Applied now: new and temporary inserts (inferences capped at 0.6; temporary items expire at the end of valid_until or after 7 days) and duplicate (adds sources, raises importance, no new version, a locked target gets only the sources); a new item with the same fingerprint as an existing memory counts as a duplicate.
